breaking.headline: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms cyberattack enabling fraudulent transactions
breaking.summary: French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed on 4 November 2026 that it was the target of a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions. The bank says the incident is now under control, some transactions were temporarily suspended, regulators and supervisory authorities have been notified, and clients face no financial consequences.
breaking.known: The bank's own statement, reported by CoinDesk, Bloomberg and Ledger Insights on 4 November, confirms the attack and the fraudulent transactions. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT first flagged a suspected loss of more than $106 million at an unnamed EU entity on 2 November and named Arkéa on 3 November, putting the total above $133 million; Bitquery traced $108.8 million in USDC withdrawals from Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX accounts over 1–2 November, and Crypto.com said it blocked funds linked to the incident.
breaking.unknown: The bank has not confirmed the amount stolen, the attack method, which system was compromised, whether the funds were fiat or cryptocurrency, or how much, if anything, has been recovered. The $133 million figure is the investigator's estimate, repeated in the press, not a bank-confirmed loss.
breaking.bfsi_impact: A named European bank victim with fraudulent transactions: peer banks should review controls on large and exchange-account withdrawals, verify transaction authorisation and suspension procedures, and watch for laundering of any linked funds through exchanges and instant-swap services. Under the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act, major ICT incidents carry a short initial reporting window, so EU-regulated peers should check their own incident-classification clocks.

entries.headline: WSO2 Open Banking CVE-2025-11969 — KEV deadline 5 November
entries.summary: Deadline watch carried from the 4 November daily brief. Not a new breaking item on 4 November itself.
entries.known: Listed in CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities with a 5 November remediation deadline, as reported in the 4 November brief.
entries.unknown: Whether affected BFSI deployments have completed remediation by the deadline — no compliance outcome was published in the brief.
entries.bfsi_impact: Open banking / API deployments using affected WSO2 versions should confirm patching before the deadline.

entries.headline: WordPress CVE-2026-119977 — KEV deadline 6 November
entries.summary: Deadline watch carried from the 4 November daily brief. Not a new breaking item on 4 November itself.
entries.known: The only new KEV entry in the 4 November brief, with a Friday 6 November deadline; patch to 7.1.4, as reported in the brief.
entries.unknown: No successful compromise via this race was publicly confirmed in the brief.
entries.bfsi_impact: WordPress estates, including marketing and customer-facing sites run by financial firms, should patch before the deadline.
